kill_risks.claim: The evidence names established categories and competitors the idea’s vocabulary omits: F5Bot is described as a free keyword-to-email tool, while GummySearch is described as an upgrade in UI; other search results list ReddiReach, RedLeads, and Reddit marketing services, indicating a broader monitoring/lead-generation category than a Chrome extension.

The buyer already has free or bundled alternatives: the evidence explicitly says F5Bot is free and simple, and the search results surface Reddit communities, Google, YouTube, Instagram, and LinkedIn as existing places where Reddit-marketing discovery and discussion happen. It does not show that users need a new extension or would pay for approved-reply drafts.

The mechanism does not establish coverage of the modal pain. It only says it activates on Reddit pages and fetches or inspects relevant public search results; the evidence does not show passive/background monitoring, reliable alert delivery, Reddit API access, or that drafting addresses the main workflow rather than merely keyword discovery.

top.name: SocialSpecLibrary
top.one_liner: Give social teams one current, source-linked truth layer for platform requirements so scheduled content keeps its channel-specific format instead of failing silently.

top.name: WikidataFeedbackHub
top.one_liner: Turn fragmented marketplace reviews into a normalized, entity-linked, category-aware backlog without manually reconciling app and company aliases.

top.name: BotSpamRegistry
top.one_liner: Give moderators a shared, evidence-linked way to recognize recurring bot accounts and reply fingerprints before automated spam makes community discussions unusable.

top.name: CoverageGap Archive
top.one_liner: Give app support and review teams an API-independent audit showing which public app conversations their live monitoring failed to capture when APIs, rate limits, or channel support changed.

top.name: ReplySieve
top.one_liner: Give community managers a human-approved queue that separates likely bot-generated replies from valuable conversation, with evidence and downloadable moderation records.

evaluated_idea.name: RedditReplyRadar
evaluated_idea.value_proposition: Give small SaaS community managers a passive Reddit discovery check and approved-reply drafts in one Chrome extension, so relevant conversations stop hiding in babysat searches and are answered faster.
evaluated_idea.mechanism_summary: Instead of starting with an always-on social listening dashboard or a standalone AI writer, RedditReplyRadar makes the browser extension itself a passive discovery checkpoint: saved queries produce a new-match badge only when the manager opens Reddit, and the same click-through…

refinement.because: Cannot keep community discussions usable when bot spam adds automated replies
